name: King of Adullam
overview: The King of Adullam was a male ruler recognized as one of thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua, as recorded in Joshua 12:15. Beyond this military defeat, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or personal background. His role is primarily noted in the context of the Israelite conquest under Joshua's leadership.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Adullam' directly identifies this individual as the ruler of Adullam. The name simply means 'king of Adullam' and does not carry additional given significance beyond this designation, as noted in Joshua 12:15.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or connections for the King of Adullam beyond his status as a defeated king listed among others in Joshua 12:15. No further relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Adullam is significant in the biblical narrative as one of the rulers subdued during the Israelite conquest of Canaan under Joshua's leadership. His defeat symbolizes the fulfillment of God's promise to give the land to Israel by removing the existing kings who opposed them. This contributes to the broader theme of divine sovereignty and Israel's obedience in securing the Promised Land.
